title: Patch parachute checkpad + telemetry playbook (72h prep) — Dec 2026 draft
checklist: Confirm patch bundle and binary hash (sha256) against release candidate
Build artifacts staged in canary cluster and smoke tests green
Telemetry baseline capture (24h pre-patch) exported to /tmp/telemetry-baseline
Prepare synthetic traffic script and runbook parameters
Notify on-call roster and establish 2-hour watch rotations
Create rollback image and verify restore script with dry-run
Unlock quiet window and block large merges across dependent repos
Prepare customer-impact comm templates and public-facing note
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, operator-focused runbook for small-medium patch windows where we need a fast rollback "parachute" if regressions appear. Emphasis on telemetry sampling that gives early signal with minimal noise. Draft status: sharing with release-ops and SRE for feedback.

Scope and assumptions:
- Patch targets the serving runtime (inference path) and a small console change.
- Expected low blast radius but potentially high latency sensitivity for tail (p99/p999).
- We run a 72-hour prep cadence (Day -3 -> Day 0) with 24h baseline capture.
- This doc is not the exhaustive postmortem — it is the day-of ops checklist and release-note stub.

Preflight (Day -3 to Day -1):
- Day -3: build + smoke
  - Verify build artifacts: sha256, container image tagged rc/patch-2026-12-01.
  - Run unit + integration smoke in staging. Fail -> stop; assign to owner.
  - Export staging telemetry snapshot to s3://redwood-release-telemetry/staging-snapshots/patch-2026-12-01.json
- Day -2: baseline capture + canary prep
  - Capture 24h baseline of key metrics (p50/p90/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token/sec, KV cache hit rate).
  - Prepare synthetic traffic harness: 1) steady low QPS (10% of prod), 2) short burst script to emulate spikes.
  - Canary config: route 2% traffic to canary cluster with identical model variant and quantization.
- Day -1: ops dry-run + comms
  - Dry-run rollback on a shadow namespace. Validate DB schema compatibility and cache warmup script.
  - Post a pre-release note to #launch-ops and notify customer success for high-risk tenants.
  - Finalize release notes stub (see section below).

Day 0 (patch window) timeline (hourly):
- T-60m: confirm watch roster (primary, secondary, SRE), set calendar beacons, set alert overrides.
- T-30m: run quick smoke on canary image (sanity checks), ensure token billing sampling enabled.
- T-10m: flip 2% traffic to canary. Monitor 10m for regressions.
- T+10m: if canary stable, increase to 10% for 20m. Observe tail latency and error rate.
- T+40m: if stable, increase to 50% for 30m. Coordinate with product on feature flags.
- T+70m: if stable, migrate remaining traffic to new image during a controlled 5-minute ramp.

Telemetry sampling plan (primary signals):
- Metrics (sample rates and aggregation windows):
  - request_latency_ms: collect at 100% for p50/p90/p95, sample 10% for full histograms every 10s bucket.
  - error_counter: 100% (alerts use 1m and 5m windows).
  - token_throughput: 100% aggregated per route every 1m.
  - kv_cache_hit_rate: 100% aggregated 1m.
  - model_fallback_count: 100% (count-based alert).
- Logs: structured logs for request traces with sampling 5% full traces, 100% metadata headers (model-id, seq-len, routing-path).
- Synthetic checks: run synthetic p95 latency check every 30s from 3 regions (us-west1, us-east1, eu-west1). Alert if p95 exceeds baseline + 30% for 2 minutes.

Decision thresholds (fast gates):
- Immediate rollback (trigger parachute) if any of:
  - sustained error rate increase >= 2x baseline and absolute error rate > 0.5% for 5 continuous minutes, OR
  - p99 latency increases > 50% relative to baseline for 5 continuous minutes, OR
  - model_fallback_count spikes by > 200 requests/minute above baseline for 3 continuous minutes, OR
  - synthetic regional p95 > baseline + 100ms for 3 consecutive checks.
- Throttled mitigation (do not rollback immediately):
  - transient spike in p95 for <3 minutes: scale canary up/down, enable traffic shaping, increase batch size if safe.

Rollback steps (parachute):
1) Announce rollback in #launch-ops with summary and immediate time stamp.
2) Flip traffic to previous stable image (image tag: stable-2026-11-28) using route-control playbook.
3) Scale down patched pods, drain gracefully, and run post-rollback smoke (5m).
4) If rollback fails to recover metrics within 10 minutes, execute escalations: paging SRE lead + incident commander.
5) Create incident stub and assign postmortem owner.

Operator cues and comms (who says what):
- Primary (release lead): Claire Nguyen — coordinates the ramp and decides on rollback.
- Secondary (SRE): Miguel Santos — verifies telemetry and executes rollback commands.
- Customer Success notifier: Priya Kapoor — drafts customer-facing note if impact > 1% of requests or > 15 min outage.
- Slack channel: #launch-ops (primary), #sre (escalation), #status (public updates if required).

Release notes (concise draft for post):
- Summary: Small runtime patch improving cache eviction stability and fixing a rare NPE in the batching layer.
- Impact: No API contract changes. Target: lower tail latency volatility under bursty loads.
- Known issues: In rare cases (long sequences >2048 tokens) there is a chance of increased memory before GC; mitigated by canary flags.
- Rollback instructions: we can revert to stable-2026-11-28; see rollback section above.

Open questions / things to confirm before day-of:
- Confirm whether any enterprise tenants have scheduled maintenance windows that conflict with our patch quiet window.
- Verify whether the console feature flag default will be toggled; if turned on, it should be gradual.
- Confirm external partner integration tests (auth proxy) are green.

Post-release notes (template):
- Time of deploy, canary percentages and ramp times, telemetry deltas (p95/p99/error rate), any mitigations applied, and final outcome (rolled forward / rolled back). Attach graphs (link to dashboards).

Appendix (operator snippets):
- Canary flip: kubectl patch service routing --type=json -p '...'
- Rollback image: helm upgrade inference --set image.tag=stable-2026-11-28 --namespace prod
- Smoke script: ./scripts/smoke-checks.sh --target canary --duration 120

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally compact for in-shift readability. Please flag anything missing or too noisy; we prefer fewer but higher-fidelity signals on small patches.
release_notes_stubs: Patch: cache-eviction-stability fixes; batching NPE fix; no API change
Risk: low — canary ramping and fast rollback configured
Rollback: stable-2026-11-28 available; see rollback playbook
